title: NASA Science
explanation:
# Rewritten for General Audience

The Moon is locked in place like a slowly spinning top, always showing Earth the same face, but spacecraft orbiting above have revealed its hidden farside—a surprisingly rough and cratered landscape that looks dramatically different from the smooth, dark plains we see from Earth. Scientists believe the farside's thicker crust acts like a tougher shell, preventing hot molten rock from welling up to the surface the way it does on the nearside, creating this starkly contrasting lunar landscape that NASA's orbiting camera has now mapped in stunning detail.
